findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 46, isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)). This requires the caller to be both admin and owner at the same time. Since those roles are exclusive, pure admins (and pure owners depending on helper semantics) will always fail the check and be denied even when they should be allowed. Consequence: legitimate team admins/owners who are not the organizer/attendee cannot add guests; authorization is broken.

findings.title: Guest deduplication and blacklist bypass via case/whitespace
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts lines 74-77, filtering does guest === attendee.email and blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) where the blacklist is lowercased but guest is not normalized or trimmed. Email comparison is therefore case-sensitive. Consequence: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS can be bypassed with different casing (e.g. Foo@spam.com vs foo@spam.com) and duplicate Attendee rows differing only by case/whitespace can be created, causing duplicate invites and blacklist evasion.

findings.title: No server-side deduplication of emails within one request
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts around line 92, the server schema is only z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check, and the handler only filters against existing attendees, not within the input itself. A payload like ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] passes the filter twice and is inserted via createMany as two Attendee rows. Consequence: duplicate attendee records, duplicate calendar invitees and duplicate emails, corrupting guest counts.

findings.title: Sends original guests list instead of filtered uniqueGuests to mailer
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 168, the handler inserts only uniqueGuests into the database but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. The mailer in packages/emails/email-manager.ts uses newGuests.includes(attendee.email) to decide between full scheduled email vs add-guests email. Consequence: pre-existing attendees re-submitted in the request are misclassified as new guests and receive the wrong template, and filtering intent is lost.

findings.title: No booking status/time guard before adding guests
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts after line 44, there is no check of booking.status, startTime or endTime before inserting attendees, updating the external calendar, and sending emails. Consequence: callers can add guests to cancelled, rejected, or long-past bookings, triggering calendar updates and confusing add-guests emails for dead events.

findings.title: Unbounded guests array allows bulk insert/email abuse
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts line 5, guests is defined as z.array(z.string().email()) with no min, max, or uniqueness limit. Consequence: a single authenticated call can submit hundreds or thousands of emails, causing a large createMany, many getTranslation lookups, a huge calendar update payload, and fan-out of emails — enabling spam and DoS.

findings.title: Calendar update uses requestor credentials instead of organizer
findings.body: In packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts line 158, credentials are loaded via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and EventManager is built from the requestor, even though the booking query already includes booking.user credentials and organizer info. If a team admin or attendee adds guests, the external calendar update runs with calendars that do not own the event. Consequence: updateCalendarAttendees fails or updates the wrong calendar, leaving external calendars out of sync while the database was already mutated.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore disableStandardEmails setting
findings.body: In packages/emails/email-manager.ts line 525, sendAddGuestsEmails takes only (calEvent, newGuests) and unconditionally sends organizer and attendee emails, unlike sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails and others which check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail. Consequence: event types or workspaces that disabled standard host/attendee emails will still send add-guests notifications, violating user settings.

findings.title: Validation error flag never cleared on success
findings.body: In apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx around line 36, onSuccess resets the email list and closes the dialog but does not reset isInvalidEmail, while Cancel does. Consequence: after one failed validation followed by a successful add, reopening the dialog still shows the stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error.
